correctness.rationale: The source one-braid construction minimizes \(N=q-h-v\) over nonnegative integers satisfying its four linear inequalities, so equivalently it maximizes \(s=h+v\). Feasibility forces \(q\ge3p-4\), attained at the boundary. In the low range \(3p-4\le q\le4p-4\), the second inequality bounds \(s\le q-3p+4\), and the displayed witnesses attain it, giving \(N=3p-4\). For \(q\ge4p-3\), adding the two oblique inequalities yields the half-sum bound on \(s\); integer parity gives the ceiling expression. When \(q\equiv2\pmod4\), equality in that half-sum bound would force the incompatible parity condition \(h-v=p\), producing exactly the one-unit penalty stated in the theorem; the supplied residue-class witnesses attain all remaining cases. An independent brute-force solution of the integer program for every coprime \(2\le p<25\), \(p<q<100\) found no mismatch with the closed form.
